key_insight: Remanent strain fields and line-like slip defects created by compression do not measurably shift or broaden the Verwey transition in stoichiometric magnetite.
engineering_relevance: Extended plastic-deformation defects can be tolerated without degrading this key electronic phase transition, unlike point defects that strongly suppress it.
method: Compressed single-crystal magnetite along [011] and [001] to create remanent defects and fracture.
Used dark-field x-ray microscopy to map defects, lattice orientation, and residual strain after unloading.
Measured ac magnetic susceptibility to track the Verwey transition temperature and sharpness.
evidence_signal: Across compressed and fractured samples, DFXM showed substantial residual disorder, but the measured Verwey transition temperature and transition sharpness were unchanged.
watch_item: The conclusion is specific to stoichiometric single-crystal magnetite and the tested loading geometries, so it may not generalize to other materials, defect types, or more severe damage states.
paper_title: Robustness of the Verwey transition against remanent strain-induced defects in magnetite
